title: "TitleCut — Implementation Plan"
date: 2026-10-07
format: html

# 1. Purpose

A native macOS app for one narrow job: take a video, scrub to points in it,
and add timed, styled titles, still frames, and zooms on those stills. It
exports a finished MP4. It is not a general video editor.

Claude Code can drive the same project through an MCP server, live, while the
app is open.

## 1.1 In scope (v1)

- Open one source video per project.
- Scrub, play, frame-step, mark points.
- Timeline of ordered segments: video ranges and still blocks.
- Split a video segment at the playhead.
- Grab the current frame as a still. Insert it as a still block for N seconds.
- Zoom keyframes on still blocks (zoom to a point, pan, ease).
- Titles: text, start, duration, style, in transition, out transition.
- Style presets, chosen before or after a title is added.
- Undo/redo for every edit, including edits made through MCP.
- Save/load project. Export MP4.
- Embedded MCP integration for Claude Code.

## 1.2 Out of scope (v1)

- Multiple source videos, multiple video tracks, picture-in-picture.
- Audio editing beyond the rule in §6.4.
- Transitions between segments (cross-dissolve etc.).
- Zoom keyframes on video segments (the model allows it later; see §4.4).
- Effects, colour grading, speed changes.
- iOS / iPad.

# 2. Platform and tooling

| Item | Value |
|---|---|
| Language | Swift 6, strict concurrency |
| UI | SwiftUI, AppKit only where SwiftUI cannot (timeline drag, key handling) |
| Media | AVFoundation, Core Image, Core Text |
| Min macOS | 26.0 (dev machine is 26.4.1, Xcode 26.5) |
| Project generation | XcodeGen (`/opt/homebrew/bin/xcodegen`), `project.yml` is the source of truth |
| Bundle ID | `com.byteclub.titlecut` |
| MCP | `modelcontextprotocol/swift-sdk` via SPM |
| Tests | Swift Testing (`@Test`), plus XCTest only where needed for performance |

::: {.callout-note}
The user handles all git operations.
:::

# 3. Architecture overview

```
┌──────────────────────────── TitleCut.app ─────────────────────────────┐
│                                                                        │
│  UI (SwiftUI)                         MCP server                       │
│  Preview · Transport · Timeline ·     tools → same commands as UI      │
│  Inspector · Style library                                             │
│           │                                   │                        │
│           └──────────────┬────────────────────┘                        │
│                          ▼                                             │
│              ProjectStore (@MainActor, @Observable)                    │
│              owns Project value + UndoManager                          │
│              every mutation = one ProjectCommand                       │
│                          │                                             │
│                          ▼                                             │
│              CompositionBuilder (pure function)                        │
│              Project → AVComposition + AVVideoComposition              │
│                          │                                             │
│           ┌──────────────┴──────────────┐                              │
│           ▼                             ▼                              │
│     AVPlayer (preview)           AVAssetExportSession (export)         │
│           └──────────────┬──────────────┘                              │
│                          ▼                                             │
│              TitleCutCompositor (AVVideoCompositing)                   │
│              draws video frame / still + zoom + titles                 │
│              via FrameRenderer (Core Image), one code path             │
└────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┘
```

## 3.1 Key principles

1. **One renderer.** Preview and export go through the same custom compositor
   and the same `FrameRenderer`. What you see is what exports.
2. **One mutation path.** UI and MCP both call `ProjectStore` commands. Nothing
   else mutates `Project`. Undo, autosave and UI refresh come for free for both.
3. **Model is value types.** `Project` is a `struct`, `Codable`, `Sendable`.
   Undo stores whole snapshots (projects are small; no diffing needed).
4. **Composition is derived.** The AV composition is rebuilt from the model
   after every change (debounced ~50 ms). It is never edited in place.

## 3.2 Module layout

Single app target, folders as logical modules. A separate framework target
(`TitleCutCore`) holds everything without UI so tests do not need the app.

```
TitleCut/
  project.yml
  CLAUDE.md
  PLAN.qmd
  App/                    TitleCutApp, AppDelegate, menus, window
  Core/                   → framework target TitleCutCore
    Model/                Project, Segment, Title, Style, Keyframe, Time
    Store/                ProjectStore, ProjectCommand, UndoSupport
    Timeline/             TimelineMath (output time ↔ segment/source time)
    Composition/          CompositionBuilder, instructions
    Render/               TitleCutCompositor, FrameRenderer, TitleRenderer,
                          StillRenderer, Easing, TransitionEvaluator
    Stills/               FrameGrabber
    Persistence/          ProjectFile (package read/write), StyleLibrary
    Export/               Exporter
  MCP/                    MCPServer, tool definitions, gate
  UI/
    Preview/              PlayerView (AVPlayerLayer host), overlay hit-testing
    Transport/            play/pause, scrub bar, timecode, frame step
    Timeline/             TimelineView, SegmentTrack, TitleTrack, Playhead
    Inspector/            TitleInspector, StillInspector, SegmentInspector
    Styles/               StylePicker, StyleEditor
    Export/               ExportSheet
  Tests/
    CoreTests/
    Fixtures/             generated test video (see §11.2)
```

# 4. Data model

All times are stored as `Tick` = `Int64` at a fixed timescale of 600
(divisible by 24, 25, 30, 60; matches `CMTime` convention). Converted to
`CMTime(value:timescale:600)` at the AVFoundation boundary. No `Double`
seconds in the model — avoids drift and float compare bugs.

```swift
struct Project: Codable, Sendable, Equatable {
    var formatVersion: Int = 1
    var source: SourceVideo
    var segments: [Segment]          // played in order
    var titles: [Title]
    var styles: [TitleStyle]         // styles used by this project (embedded copies)
    var stills: [StillImage]         // images captured into the package
    var output: OutputSettings
}

struct SourceVideo: Codable, Sendable, Equatable {
    var bookmark: Data               // file bookmark to the original video
    var lastKnownPath: String
    var duration: Tick
    var naturalSize: CGSize
    var frameRate: Double            // nominal, for frame-step
}

enum Segment: Codable, Sendable, Equatable, Identifiable {
    case video(VideoSegment)
    case still(StillSegment)
}

struct VideoSegment: Codable, Sendable, Equatable {
    var id: UUID
    var sourceRange: TickRange       // range in the source video
}

struct StillSegment: Codable, Sendable, Equatable {
    var id: UUID
    var stillID: UUID                // → Project.stills
    var duration: Tick
    var zoom: [ZoomKeyframe]         // empty = static full frame
}

struct StillImage: Codable, Sendable, Equatable {
    var id: UUID
    var fileName: String             // stills/<id>.png inside the package
    var capturedAt: Tick?            // source time it was grabbed from, if any
    var pixelSize: CGSize
}

struct ZoomKeyframe: Codable, Sendable, Equatable {
    var time: Tick                   // relative to segment start
    var center: CGPoint              // normalised 0…1 in image space
    var scale: Double                // 1.0 = full frame, 2.0 = 2× zoom
    var easing: Easing               // easing INTO this keyframe
}

struct Title: Codable, Sendable, Equatable, Identifiable {
    var id: UUID
    var text: String
    var anchor: TitleAnchor
    var duration: Tick
    var styleID: UUID
    var styleOverrides: StyleOverrides?   // per-title tweaks (position, size)
    var transitionIn: Transition
    var transitionOut: Transition
}

struct TitleAnchor: Codable, Sendable, Equatable {
    var segmentID: UUID
    var offset: Tick                 // from segment start
}

struct Transition: Codable, Sendable, Equatable {
    var kind: TransitionKind         // .none .fade .slide(edge) .scale .typewriter
    var duration: Tick
    var easing: Easing
}

enum Easing: String, Codable, Sendable { case linear, easeIn, easeOut, easeInOut }

struct TitleStyle: Codable, Sendable, Equatable, Identifiable {
    var id: UUID
    var name: String
    var fontName: String
    var fontSizeRatio: Double        // fraction of output height (resolution-independent)
    var weight: FontWeight
    var textColor: RGBA
    var background: BackgroundBox?   // colour, padding, corner radius
    var shadow: Shadow?
    var stroke: Stroke?
    var alignment: TextAlignment
    var position: NormalizedPosition // preset (lowerThird, center, top…) or custom x/y
    var maxWidthRatio: Double        // wrap width as fraction of output width
}

struct OutputSettings: Codable, Sendable, Equatable {
    var size: CGSize                 // default = source naturalSize
    var frameRate: Double            // default = source
    var codec: Codec                 // .h264 / .hevc
}
```

## 4.1 Why titles anchor to segments

A title placed at absolute output time 0:12 would drift onto the wrong
content when a still is inserted before it. Anchoring to `(segmentID,
offset)` keeps it on its content. When a segment is split, titles anchored to
it are re-anchored to whichever half contains their start. When a segment is
deleted, its titles are deleted with it (undoable).

::: {.callout-important}
This is a design decision for the user to confirm — see §13, D1.
:::

## 4.2 Timeline math (`TimelineMath`)

Pure functions, fully unit tested:

- `outputDuration(project)`
- `segmentStart(id) -> Tick` (output time)
- `locate(outputTime) -> (segmentID, offsetInSegment)`
- `sourceTime(outputTime) -> Tick?` (nil inside a still)
- `titleOutputRange(title) -> TickRange`
- `split(segmentID, at offset) -> (Segment, Segment)`
- Clamping: titles may extend past their segment end into following
  segments; they are clamped only to total output duration.

## 4.3 Stills

- Grab: `AVAssetImageGenerator` with `requestedTimeToleranceBefore/After =
  .zero`, `appliesPreferredTrackTransform = true`, at the current *source*
  time. Saved as PNG into the package `stills/` folder.
- Grab is only valid while the playhead is inside a video segment.
- Insert: splits the current video segment at the playhead and inserts the
  still segment between the halves. Default duration 3 s (configurable).
- Still segments can also be dragged to another position in the timeline.

## 4.4 Zoom keyframes

- Evaluated per frame: find surrounding keyframes, interpolate `center` and
  `scale` with the later keyframe's easing.
- Before the first keyframe: hold first value. After the last: hold last.
- With zero keyframes: full frame, scale 1.
- The visible rect is clamped so it never leaves the image (no black edges).
- The `ZoomKeyframe` type is segment-agnostic so video segments can use it
  later without a model change.

# 5. Persistence

## 5.1 Project file

A document package `MyEdit.titlecut/` (directory shown as one file in Finder):

```
MyEdit.titlecut/
  project.json
  stills/
    <uuid>.png
```

- Implemented with SwiftUI `DocumentGroup` + `FileDocument`/`ReferenceFileDocument`
  using `FileWrapper` for the package.
- The source video is **referenced**, not copied (videos are large). Stored as
  a bookmark plus last known path. If the file is missing on open, show a
  relink dialog.
- `formatVersion` checked on load; unknown higher version refuses to open
  with a clear message.
- Autosave via the document system.

## 5.2 Style library

- App-wide presets in `~/Library/Application Support/TitleCut/styles.json`.
- Ships with a built-in set (e.g. Lower Third, Centered Bold, Caption,
  Chapter Card, Minimal).
- When a style is applied to a title, the style is copied into
  `Project.styles` so the project renders identically on another machine or
  after the library changes.
- Editing a project style offers "update in library too".
- Built 2026-10-14: a title's customised copy of a library style records
  it (`TitleStyle.basedOn`). CUSTOMISE then offers UPDATE <NAME>, which
  writes the look over the library style and gives it to every title on that
  style in this project; other projects keep their embedded copies.
  Right-clicking a tile in the STYLES panel renames a style, deletes a saved
  one, or reverts a changed built-in.

# 6. Rendering

## 6.1 Composition build

`CompositionBuilder.build(project) -> (AVMutableComposition, AVMutableVideoComposition)`

- One video composition track, one audio composition track.
- Video segment → `insertTimeRange(sourceRange, of: sourceTrack, at: cursor)`.
- Still segment → `insertEmptyTimeRange(...)` on both tracks; the compositor
  produces the frame itself.
- One `TitleCutInstruction` (conforming to `AVVideoCompositionInstructionProtocol`)
  per segment, covering that segment's output range. Each instruction carries
  an immutable snapshot of what is needed to draw it: segment kind, still image
  reference, zoom keyframes, the titles overlapping its range, the styles.
- `videoComposition.customVideoCompositorClass = TitleCutCompositor.self`.
- Render size and frame duration from `OutputSettings`.
- Source preferred transform (rotated phone video) applied in the compositor.

## 6.2 Compositor (`TitleCutCompositor`)

- Implements `AVVideoCompositing`. Runs on its own serial queue.
- For each request: read the instruction, get the source frame (video
  segments) or the cached still `CIImage` (still segments), hand both to
  `FrameRenderer`, render into a pixel buffer from the render context pool.
- A shared `CIContext` (Metal-backed) for the life of the compositor.
- Still images decoded once and cached by `stillID`.
- `cancelAllPendingVideoCompositionRequests` honoured (scrubbing generates many).

## 6.3 FrameRenderer

`render(base: CIImage, at outputTime, context) -> CIImage`

1. Base: source frame with preferred transform, scaled/letterboxed to output
   size; or still with zoom rect cropped and scaled to output size.
2. Titles active at this time, in order of start time:
   - Text laid out with Core Text into a `CGImage` (cached per title + style
     + render size; cache invalidates on any change).
   - Transition evaluated → opacity, offset, scale, character count
     (typewriter).
   - Composited over the base with `CIFilter.sourceOverCompositing` after an
     affine transform.
3. Pure enough to call outside AVFoundation — used by tests and by the MCP
   `render_frame` tool.

## 6.4 Audio during stills

Stills insert silence: the source audio pauses with the video and resumes
after. (Alternative in §13, D3.)

## 6.5 Preview

- `AVPlayer` with an `AVPlayerItem` built from the composition +
  video composition. Rebuilt when the model changes, preserving playhead time
  and play state.
- Scrubbing: `seek(to:toleranceBefore:.zero, toleranceAfter:.zero)` while
  dragging, with coalescing (only the latest pending seek is issued).
- Frame step: `AVPlayerItem.step(byCount:)`.

# 7. UI

## 7.1 Window layout

```
┌──────────────────────────────────────────────┬──────────────┐
│                                              │              │
│               Preview                        │  Inspector   │
│        (click a title to select it)          │  (selected   │

├──────────────────────────────────────────────┤              │
│ ◀◀ ▶ ▶▶   00:01:12:05 / 00:03:40:00   [scrub] │              │
├──────────────────────────────────────────────┴──────────────┤
│ Titles   ▭▭▭▭     ▭▭▭        ▭▭▭▭▭▭                         │
│ Segments ███████████|▒▒still▒▒|██████████████████            │
│                     ▲ playhead                              │
└─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┘
```

## 7.2 Actions and shortcuts

| Action | Shortcut | Notes |
|---|---|---|
| Play / pause | Space | |
| Frame back / forward | ← / → | |
| 1 s back / forward | ⇧← / ⇧→ | |
| Add title at playhead | T | uses current default style |
| Grab still | S | only inside a video segment |
| Insert grabbed still at playhead | ⇧S | |
| Split segment at playhead | ⌘K | |
| Add zoom keyframe at playhead | Z | only inside a still segment |
| Delete selection | ⌫ | |
| Undo / redo | ⌘Z / ⇧⌘Z | |
| Export | ⌘E | |

## 7.3 Timeline

- Segment track: video segments as solid blocks with thumbnail strip
  (generated lazily via `AVAssetImageGenerator`), stills as image-filled
  blocks.
- Title track: one lane; overlapping titles stack into extra lanes
  automatically.
- Drag title body = move (re-anchors on drop). Drag title edges = duration.
- Drag still block edges = duration. Drag still block = reorder.
- Click anywhere = move playhead. Zoom timeline with pinch / ⌘+ ⌘−.
- Implemented as a SwiftUI `Canvas` for drawing plus gesture handling; drop to
  an `NSView` only if gesture handling proves inadequate.

## 7.4 Inspector

- **Title:** text field (multi-line), style picker (thumbnails), duration,
  in/out transition pickers with duration and easing, position override.
- **Still segment:** duration, zoom keyframe list, "add keyframe at
  playhead", per-keyframe centre (drag a reticle on the preview) and scale.
- **Video segment:** source in/out (read-only timecodes), split, delete.

## 7.5 Styles

- Style picker shows live thumbnails rendered by `TitleRenderer`.
- "Default style for new titles" setting — the "pre-pick" case.
- Changing a title's style afterwards re-renders immediately — the
  "pick after" case.
- Multi-select titles → apply style to all.

# 8. Undo

- `ProjectStore` holds `project: Project` and an `UndoManager`.
- `perform(_ command: ProjectCommand)` snapshots the old value, applies, and
  registers an undo action restoring the snapshot, named for the menu
  ("Undo Add Title").
- Continuous gestures (dragging a title) coalesce into one undo step via
  `beginGesture` / `endGesture`.
- MCP commands go through `perform` too, so ⌘Z undoes Claude's edits.

# 9. Export

- `AVAssetExportSession` with the built composition and video composition.
- Presets: H.264 or HEVC at output size. Output `.mp4`.
- Uses the modern async `export(to:as:)` API with progress observation.
- Export sheet: destination, codec, progress bar, cancel.
- On failure: show what failed and what to do (the user started it, so it may
  speak). No messages for background work.

# 10. MCP integration

## 10.1 Transport

Claude Code must reach a server living inside a running GUI app. Two options:

- **A — Stdio bridge (recommended).** A small command-line tool
  `titlecut-mcp`, built in the same project and embedded in the app bundle
  (`TitleCut.app/Contents/MacOS/titlecut-mcp`). Claude Code launches it via
  stdio (`StdioTransport` from the Swift SDK — confirmed supported). It
  forwards each tool call to the running app over a Unix domain socket at
  `~/Library/Application Support/TitleCut/mcp.sock`. If the app is not
  running, tools return "TitleCut is not running. Open it and retry."
  Registration: `claude mcp add titlecut -- /Applications/TitleCut.app/Contents/MacOS/titlecut-mcp`
- **B — In-app HTTP server.** Only if the Swift SDK ships a server-side HTTP
  transport. Not confirmed — a search found only `HTTPClientTransport`.
  Verify in `Sources/MCP` before choosing.

::: {.callout-important}
Transport choice is for the user to confirm — see §13, D4.
:::

## 10.2 Gate

Per the standing MCP rule: a `get_instructions()` tool returns the full
description, tool list and an example workflow, and sets a flag. Every other
tool returns
`"Call get_instructions() first to initialize this MCP server before using any other tools."`
until it has been called. The flag lives in the bridge process (resets with
each Claude Code session).

## 10.3 Tools

All times in tools are seconds (Double) for readability; converted to
`Tick` at the boundary. All IDs are UUID strings.

| Tool | Purpose |
|---|---|
| `get_instructions` | gate + documentation |
| `get_project` | source info, output duration, segments, titles, styles (JSON) |
| `open_video(path)` | start a new project from a video |
| `get_playhead` / `seek(seconds)` | read / move the playhead |
| `list_segments` | ordered segments with output start/end |
| `split_segment(at_seconds)` | split at an output time |
| `delete_segment(id)` | |
| `grab_still(at_seconds)` | capture source frame → still ID |
| `insert_still(still_id, at_seconds, duration)` | insert still block |
| `set_segment_duration(id, seconds)` | stills only |
| `add_zoom_keyframe(segment_id, at, center_x, center_y, scale, easing)` | |
| `remove_zoom_keyframe(segment_id, index)` | |
| `list_titles` | with resolved output times |
| `add_title(text, at_seconds, duration, style?, in?, out?)` | |
| `update_title(id, fields…)` | partial update |
| `delete_title(id)` | |
| `list_styles` / `set_title_style(title_ids, style)` | |
| `render_frame(at_seconds)` | PNG of the composed frame, so Claude can see the result |
| `export(path, codec)` / `export_status` | start export, poll progress |
| `undo` / `redo` | |

Every mutating tool calls the same `ProjectStore` command the UI uses, on the
main actor, and returns the changed entity as JSON.

::: {.callout-note}
MCP scope (agreed 2026-10-14). Everything the UI can do is a tool. The table
above is superseded by this list.

- Transport (revised 2026-10-14): the app serves MCP Streamable HTTP at
  `http://127.0.0.1:PORT/mcp` (SDK `StatefulHTTPServerTransport`, one MCP
  session per Claude Code session, gate per session). This Mac only, and
  with "Require key" on, every request must carry the key as
  `Authorization: Bearer <key>` (kept in the login keychain; New key in the
  panel replaces it). The switch is saved. **It defaults to off for now, while
  debug builds re-sign on every build; turn the default on before release.** The instructions
  also go out in the initialize handshake. An MCP button right of Export
  turns it on: grey off, green listening; off the first time, then as it
  was at quit. The port is remembered (default 7340); if taken, the next free
  one is used and the panel says so. The panel shows the key, the
  `claude mcp add --transport http … --header` command and the address. The
  stdio helper is removed. The app must be open.
- Target: the front project window by default. `list_projects` names the open
  projects; every tool takes an optional `project` to pick another.
- Each tool call is one undo step, named as the UI names it, so ⌘Z undoes it.

Tools, by area:

- Session: `get_instructions` (gate), `list_projects`, `get_project`,
  `undo`, `redo`, `save`.
- `get_project` is the full snapshot, as JSON: source file (path, length,
  size, frame rate, audio or not), shape and output length, playhead,
  selection, saved state, what Undo and Redo would do; every clip with output
  and source times, framing, and freeze camera; every title with resolved
  times, text and full look; every music piece; whether a transcript exists;
  export progress.
- Video and shape: `open_video(path)`, `set_shape(16:9 | 9:16 | 1:1 |
  original)`, `get_playhead`, `seek(seconds)`, `play`, `pause`.
- Clips: `list_segments`, `split_at(seconds)`, `delete_segment`,
  `move_segment(id, to_seconds)`, `trim_segment(id, start, end)` (source
  range), `set_framing(id, framing?, y?, zoom?)`, `set_split(id, split?,
  first?, second?, first_y?, first_zoom?, second_y?, second_zoom?)`, `freeze_frame(at_seconds, duration)`,
  `set_freeze_length(id, seconds)`, `set_camera(id, center_x, center_y,
  scale, pace)`, `reset_camera(id)`.
- Titles: `list_titles`, `add_title(text, at, duration?, style?)`,
  `update_title(id, text?, start?, duration?, position?, size?, look…,
  transition_in?, transition_out?)`, `delete_titles(ids)`,
  `duplicate_titles(ids)`, `set_titles_style(ids, style)`, `list_styles`.
- Captions: `auto_captions(language?, style?)` (runs transcription, reports
  progress), `get_transcript` (words with times), `list_captions`,
  `export_subtitles(path)`.
- Silences: `find_silences(quieter_than_db, longer_than_seconds)` (dry run:
  count, seconds removed, the ranges), `remove_silences(same settings)`.
- Music: `add_music(path, at?)`, `list_music`, `update_music(id, start?,
  song_start?, duration?, volume?, fade_in?, fade_out?)`, `delete_music`,
  `duplicate_music`.
- Output: `render_frame(at_seconds)` (PNG, so Claude can see the result),
  `export(path, codec, subtitles?)`, `export_status`.
:::

# 11. Testing

## 11.1 Unit tests (TitleCutCore)

- `TimelineMath`: locate, split, title re-anchoring on split/delete,
  output duration, boundary cases (time exactly on a segment edge).
- Zoom interpolation: before/between/after keyframes, each easing, clamping
  the visible rect inside the image.
- Transition evaluation: opacity/offset at start, mid, end of in and out;
  titles shorter than in+out durations (transitions scaled down, never
  overlap).
- Codable round trip of `Project`; refusal of a higher `formatVersion`.
- Undo: every command undoes to an `Equatable`-identical project.

## 11.2 Render tests

- Fixture video generated at test time with `AVAssetWriter`: 5 s, 640×360,
  30 fps, each frame a solid colour that encodes its frame number. No binary
  fixtures committed.
- Build composition for a known project, pull frames with
  `AVAssetImageGenerator` using the video composition, assert:
  - correct source frame appears at the right output time after a still,
  - still segment frame matches the grabbed image,
  - a title pixel region is non-background while active and background
    outside its range.
- Export test: export the fixture project, assert output duration equals
  `TimelineMath.outputDuration`.

## 11.3 MCP tests

- Gate: every tool except `get_instructions` returns the gate message first.
- Each tool against an in-memory `ProjectStore`: mutation result and undo.

# 12. Milestones

Each milestone ends with tests passing and the app runnable. The user QAs
before the next starts.

| # | Milestone | Done when |
|---|---|---|
| M0 | Scaffold | `project.yml`, app + `TitleCutCore` + tests + `titlecut-mcp` targets, builds and runs an empty window |
| M1 | Open and scrub | open video, preview, play/pause, scrub, frame step, timecode |
| M2 | Model and timeline | `Project` model, `TimelineMath`, segment track, split, delete, undo, save/load package |
| M3 | Compositor | custom compositor drives preview; video segments render identically to M1 |
| M4 | Titles | add/move/resize titles, inspector, built-in styles, all transitions, preview |
| M5 | Stills | grab, insert, duration, reorder, audio silence during stills |
| M6 | Zoom | keyframes, inspector, reticle on preview, easing |
| M7 | Export | export sheet, progress, cancel, render/export tests |
| M8 | MCP | bridge, socket, gate, all tools, `render_frame` |
| M9 | Polish | thumbnails strip, style editor, relink missing video, shortcuts audit |

::: {.callout-important}
Scope change (2026-10-08): v1 is titles-only. Build order after M3 is
M4, M7, M8, M9. M5 (Stills) and M6 (Zoom) are deferred past v1.
:::

::: {.callout-note}
Trim (added 2026-10-13, built alongside M7). Every video segment is a range
of the whole source, so its edges can be dragged in (trim) or out (reveal
hidden source), never past the source's start or end.

- Ripple: a segment's length change shifts every later segment; no gaps, no
  overlaps.
- Titles stick to the footage: extending or trimming the left edge by `d`
  changes their anchor offset by `d`, so they stay on the same source frame.
- A title whose start would fall outside the trimmed segment is clamped to
  the segment's nearest edge.
- One command, `trimSegment`; an edge drag is one undo step.
:::

::: {.callout-note}
Moving clips and gaps (agreed 2026-10-13). Supersedes "always ripple" above.

- New segment kind `gap` (a duration, no media): renders black with silence.
  Encoded as `{"gap":{...}}`; formatVersion stays 1 (nothing shipped yet).
- Dragging a clip body moves it. Titles anchored to it move with it.
- Dropping onto another clip inserts it there and pushes later clips right;
  nothing ever overlaps. Space it leaves behind becomes a gap.
- Trimming an edge first eats into or opens the adjacent gap; it pushes later
  clips only when no gap is left. Adjacent gaps merge; a trailing gap is
  dropped.
- Magnetic snapping while dragging a clip or an edge: clip edges, the
  playhead and the timeline start, within a few points on screen.
- Titles can anchor to a gap (e.g. an intro title over black).
- Each drag is one undo step.
- Changed 2026-10-15, Final Cut style: lifting a clip closes up its place
  (moves never leave a gap), and the drop is measured on the timeline
  without it. On another clip it goes in at the nearer edge and later clips
  slide right live; in a gap it takes that place; past the end it is
  appended.
:::

::: {.callout-note}
Transcription (agreed 2026-10-13, after M8). On-device speech-to-text with
word timings (macOS 26 speech APIs; no cloud, no key). Uses: auto-captions
(each phrase becomes a timed title), and a transcript exposed through the MCP
bridge so Claude can propose titles, chapter cards and silence cuts. Details
to be planned when M8 is done.

Auto-captions (brought forward, agreed 2026-10-13):

- The transcript is saved in the package as `transcript.json` (source-time
  words with start/end), so transcription runs once per source.
- Captions are short lines: up to about 7 words / 42 characters / 3 s, broken
  at pauses and sentence ends. Only speech inside kept segments becomes
  captions, anchored to the segment it falls in.
- Titles made by auto-captions carry a marker. Running it again replaces the
  marked titles (one undo step); hand-made titles are untouched.

Word highlight and SRT (agreed 2026-10-14):

- Auto-captions store their words with times relative to the title start
  (optional field on Title). Styles get an optional highlight (on/off,
  colour). The spoken word changes to the highlight colour.
- SRT export contains the auto-captions as they are on the timeline, at
  output times. Export sheet checkbox "Also save subtitles (.srt)" and
  File > Export Subtitles….

Ideas to review:

- Transitions between clips (added to the to-do list 2026-10-14, after MCP):
  crossfade or dip to black at a cut. Built 2026-10-14: dips, fades and
  crossfades at cuts, the start and the end, without changing the video's
  length.
- Mass edit of transitions (backlog, nice to have, 2026-10-14): change the
  kind or length of many transitions at once, or put one at every cut.
- Filler-word removal (backlog, 2026-10-15): find "um", "uh" and similar in
  the transcript and cut them, with a dry run like find_silences. Built
  2026-10-15 (`FillerRemoval`): sounds only (um, uh, er, ah, hmm and
  variants), never words such as "like". Timeline > Remove Filler Words…
  uses the saved transcript, or transcribes only when the person presses
  Transcribe (shared with Auto-Captions as `Transcription`). Auto-captions
  are rebuilt in the same undo step. MCP: find_fillers, remove_fillers.
- Face reframing (backlog, 2026-10-15): track the speaker's face and keep it
  framed when the output shape is narrower than the source, such as 9:16.
  Built 2026-10-15 as Frame Faces (`FaceFraming`): the largest face is
  sampled every 0.25 s (at most 400 frames a clip). Where it settles more
  than a quarter of the frame's width away for 1 s or longer, the clip is
  split there; each part is framed on the median position. One undo step.
  Clips without a face keep theirs. FRAME FACES under the framing map,
  Timeline > Frame Faces, MCP frame_faces. A framing that pans with the
  face was not chosen.
- Title cards (built 2026-10-15): a segment kind `card` (`CardSegment`:
  length, solid colour, transitions), silent, for titles on a plain
  background. Not a gap: gaps are empty space that trims eat, merge and drop
  at the end. Inserted black and 3 s long at the playhead (+ > Card,
  Timeline > Insert Title Card), without a title; at a cut it takes the cut's
  transition, inside a clip it splits it. The inspector sets its colour and
  length; its ends drag like a freeze's. MCP: insert_card, set_card. Later:
  an image background.
- Animated GIF export (built 2026-10-16, `GIFExporter`): a Format chip
  (MP4 / GIF) in the Export sheet. GIF options: Loop Forever / Once, width
  320 / 480 / 720 px (height follows the shape), 10 / 15 / 24 fps. Whole
  video, no sound, same frames and watermark as MP4, written with ImageIO.
  MCP export takes format (default from the extension), loop, gif_width,
  gif_fps. File > Export… and the Export button replace "Export MP4".
- Clip speed and volume (built 2026-10-16): `VideoSegment.speed` (0.5,
  0.75, 1, 1.25, 1.5, 2; `nil` is 1) and `volume` (0...2; `nil` is 1), absent
  from older files. Speed sets the clip's timeline length; source time maps
  through `sourceOffset(atOutput:)` / `outputOffset(ofSource:)` in splits,
  trims, captions, silences, fillers, Frame Faces, crossfade handles and the
  waveform. Speech keeps its pitch (spectral). Titles on a clip keep their
  footage when its speed changes; auto-captions also scale their length and
  words. Selecting a video clip shows the CLIP inspector (speed chips,
  volume slider with Mute). MCP: set_clip; get_project shows speed, volume.
- More videos on one timeline (built 2026-10-18): Add Video puts a whole
  video at the end as one clip, on the same single track, to split, trim
  and move like any clip. `Project.addedSources` holds the videos after the
  first, each with an ID; `VideoSegment.sourceID` names a clip's video
  (`nil` is `Project.source`), absent from older files. A file already in
  the project is reused; a video no clip plays is removed. The first video
  sets the output size and frame rate; others fill the frame, cropped, with
  framing as usual. One composition track takes every clip from its own
  file. Transcripts are kept per video in `transcripts.json` (older
  packages' `transcript.json` is read); captions, silences, fillers and
  Frame Faces work per clip's video. A missing video shows Video Not Found
  with Locate Video for that file. Entry points: File > Add Video…
  (Option-Command-O), + > Video at End…, dropping a file on the timeline,
  MCP add_video; get_project lists added_videos and each clip's video.
- Split screen (built 2026-10-19): a video clip can show two parts of its
  picture at once, each filling half the frame, e.g. an interviewer on top
  and the guest below in 9:16. `VideoSegment.split` (`SplitScreen`: `first`
  and `second` framings, 0...1 like `framing`), absent from older files;
  `framing` is unused while it is set. Since 2026-10-22 each half is a
  `ClipFraming` (x, y, zoom) and boxes zoom 1-6x (1-3x until 2026-10-23); see below. The halves are equal: stacked in a
  frame at least as tall as wide (first on top), side by side in a wider
  one (first on the left). CLIP inspector > Screen:
  WHOLE / SPLIT (starts at 0.25 and 0.75); the framing map shows boxes 1
  and 2 to drag; Command-dragging the preview moves the half pressed. Both
  parts of a cut keep it. Freeze Frame joins both halves into the still.
  Frame Faces leaves split clips alone. MCP: set_split; get_project shows
  split.
  Zoom and vertical framing (built 2026-10-22): boxes zoom 1-6x through
  corner handles in the framing map and move in x and y, for whole clips and
  split halves (`ClipFraming`: x, y, zoom; `VideoSegment.framingY` and `zoom`,
  absent from older files; older split files with numbers load as x).
  Command-drag moves in 2D. Frame Faces sets x only and accounts for zoom.
  MCP: set_framing gains y and zoom; set_split gains first_y, first_zoom,
  second_y, second_zoom; get_project shows framing_y, zoom and split halves
  as objects.
  Timeline: a split clip shows a dashed line between its halves and a
  "Split" tag (2026-10-23).
  Built and removed 2026-10-23: a half showing another video (per-segment
  feeds meant cutting at every switch), and a half holding a frame while
  the other plays (one clock per clip, so a paused half cannot resume
  where it stopped; the halves drift apart).
- Generated music (not chosen, 2026-10-16): an optional ElevenLabs or Gemini
  key to make background music in the app. Skipped as duplication: people
  with a key can generate a track there and use Add Music, and over MCP
  Claude can pair the provider's own MCP server with add_music. MusicGen
  on device was ruled out by its non-commercial weights licence.
- AI frame image (backlog, 2026-10-15): send a frame and a prompt to an
  image model (OpenAI or Google Gemini; Claude does not make images) with
  the person's own API key, and insert the result as a freeze at that frame.

- Live caption strip: while the video plays, the words being spoken show as
  a caption. Clicking a word, or selecting a run of words, makes a title from
  them, timed to when they are spoken.
- Signing (decided 2026-10-14): Debug builds are signed with the Apple
  Development certificate (set in an uncommitted Config/Local.xcconfig), so the code identity survives
  rebuilds and macOS keeps the Open Recent list. Release stays ad-hoc until
  the purchasing work moves it to the App Sandbox.
:::

::: {.callout-note}
Paid unlock (agreed 2026-10-14, purchasing not built yet). The app is a free
download. Exports carry a large see-through "TitleCut" wordmark across the
middle of every frame (`Watermark`, built). A one-time purchase of about
$2.99 removes it.

- StoreKit 2, one non-consumable in-app purchase, plus Restore Purchases.
- Unlocked means `Transaction.currentEntitlements` holds a `.verified`
  transaction for that product (signed by Apple, checked on the Mac). Nothing
  is cached in user defaults or the project.
- The check runs at export time and feeds `Exporter.export(watermark:)`.
  Built 2026-10-14 (`App/Purchase/Unlock.swift`): product
  `com.byteclub.titlecut.unlock`, bought or restored from the export sheet;
  MCP exports use the same check. Local testing uses
  `StoreKit/TitleCut.storekit`, which applies only when run from Xcode.
- The wordmark is drawn inside the export render, not as a separate layer.
- Requires Mac App Store distribution and the App Sandbox, which reverses D5
  (unsandboxed, ad-hoc). Source access then needs security-scoped bookmarks.
- Sandbox built 2026-10-14 (`App/TitleCut.entitlements`): user-selected
  files, security-scoped bookmarks, network server. Source videos are
  bookmarked with security scope; a project whose video the app may not open
  shows Video Not Found with Locate Video. MCP tools use paths only inside
  folders the person allows (MCP panel > Folders, `MCPFolders`), and
  inside ~/Movies and ~/Music, which the entitlements grant. The .srt
  beside an export is written as a related item. Debug builds from Xcode get
  an injected read-only exception for `/`, so reading is not sandboxed there;
  `CODE_SIGN_INJECT_BASE_ENTITLEMENTS=NO` builds without it.
:::

::: {.callout-note}
Full title customisation (agreed 2026-10-13, phase two, with the M9 style
editor). Font, size, weight, text colour, background box, shadow, outline,
alignment and wrap width, editable in the right-hand panel and savable as a
style. `TitleStyle` already stores all of these.
:::

# 13. Open decisions for the user

Defaults below are what the plan assumes. Confirm or change before the
relevant milestone.

| ID | Decision | Default in this plan | Alternative |
|---|---|---|---|
| D1 | Title anchoring | anchored to segment + offset (§4.1) | absolute output time |
| D2 | Title renderer | Core Image inside the custom compositor, one path for preview and export (§6) | Core Animation layers (`AVVideoCompositionCoreAnimationTool` for export, `AVSynchronizedLayer` for preview). This was the earlier proposal; it gives two code paths and does not cover stills/zoom. |
| D3 | Audio during stills | silence; source audio resumes after | source audio keeps playing under the still (video and audio drift apart) |
| D4 | MCP transport | **In-app HTTP on 127.0.0.1 (decided 2026-10-14, replacing the stdio bridge built the same day)** | stdio bridge + Unix socket |
| D5 | Sandboxing / distribution | unsandboxed, local build only (sandbox complicates the socket and bookmarks) | App Sandbox + Developer ID / App Store |
| D6 | Source video storage | referenced by bookmark | copied into the package |
| D7 | Min macOS | 26.0 | 15.0 for wider reach |
| D8 | About screen / DEV-PROD build split (the iOS project convention) | not included | add an About window with version and build date |
| D9 | Release script / CI | none (macOS, local use) | `scripts/release.sh` per the iOS convention |
